title: Exploring communication between people living with Motor Neurone Disease and their close persons with healthcare professionals
official: Exploring communication between people living with Motor Neurone Disease and their close persons with healthcare professionals: a longitudinal qualitative study
summary:
Background and study aims
Motor Neurone Disease (MND) affects how people move, speak, and eventually breathe. As the illness progresses, it becomes harder for people to communicate, especially near the end of life. This can make it difficult to plan care and make important decisions. This study aims to understand how people with MND and their close family or friends communicate with healthcare professionals. We want to learn what helps and what makes communication harder, so we can improve how care is delivered. The goal is to create a toolkit to help healthcare professionals communicate better with people living with MND.

Who can participate?
We are inviting people who have been diagnosed with MND, their close family members or friends, and healthcare professionals involved in their care.

What does the study involve?
Participants will be asked to take part in up to three interviews over time (every 4–6 months or until the person with MND passes away). These interviews will explore their experiences of communication with healthcare professionals. We will also observe around 10 clinical appointments to see how conversations happen in real life. This will help us understand how language is used during care discussions.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating?
Taking part may help improve communication for others living with MND in the future. There are no major risks, but talking about illness and end-of-life care can sometimes be emotional. Support will be available if needed.

Where is the study run from?
University of Birmingham (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for?
September 2025 to August 2027

Who is funding the study?
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK). 

Who is the main contact?
Prof. Cara Bailey, c.bailey.2@bham.ac.uk

interventions.name: The research allows for a longitudinal design of data collection to occur over 12 months at three different time points per patient case, approximately 4 to 6 months apart. The research design, based on a previous study, will capture the patients’ journey, highlighting good examples of communication

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients and carers:
1.	Adults (over 18 years)
2.	Able to make decision of informed consent to take part in the study
3.	Able to participate in an interview (written or spoken)
4.	Receiving or received specialist service from the Hospital Based Centre or hospice

Primary care healthcare professional interviews:
1.	Working in a participating site supporting delivery of Motor Neurone Disease services.
Exclusion criteria:
1.	Unable to consent
2.	Medically too unwell to participate or otherwise deemed unsuitable for participation by clinical team
3.	Expressed a wish not to be contacted or involved in research
4.	Children and young people under the age of 18 years old
